Sundhedsklynge Sønderjylland is a healthcare cluster operating within [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] in Denmark. It is actively monitored in the national quality reports for the treatment of [[atrieflimren]] (AFDK) published by the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP) and the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute. The cluster's performance is evaluated across multiple clinical quality indicators, revealing a mix of standard compliance and areas requiring significant improvement.

In terms of anticoagulation treatment initiation, Sundhedsklynge Sønderjylland successfully met the national standard for Indicator 1, achieving a result of 92.6% for the timely initiation of therapy in newly diagnosed patients [^src1]. However, the cluster's performance varies considerably across other metrics. For [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]], which measures the clinical practice of performing TSH measurements at the time of a new diagnosis to rule out thyroid disease, the cluster recorded the lowest performance among all health clusters at 41.2% in the 2025 reporting period [^src10]. This significantly lower result was attributed to the use of local laboratory codes for TSH measurements, which prevented the data from being captured and transferred to the national SundK database [^src10]. In the 2024 reporting period, the variation in target fulfillment for this indicator across all health clusters ranged from 52.9% in Sundhedsklynge Sønderjylland to 87.9% in [[horsensklyngen|Horsensklyngen]] [^src14].

Regarding patient education, the cluster is working towards the national standard for [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], which tracks the proportion of newly diagnosed patients receiving structured patient education within the first year. With a recorded value of 40.7% in the 2025 report [^src11] and 42.5% in the 2024 report, Sundhedsklynge Sønderjylland is noted as being relatively close to fulfilling the standard, alongside [[randersklyngen|Randersklyngen]] [^src5]. 

Furthermore, the cluster is included in national geographic distributions and supplementary analyses, such as the incidence of apoplexy (stroke) among patients, which is mapped at the health cluster level [^src4]. It is also tracked for outcomes like severe bleeding, heart failure, and mortality, contributing to the broader hierarchical quality improvement strategy in the Danish healthcare system [^src6] [^src7] [^src8].
